items.stem: How do jobs within the same stage of a GitLab CI pipeline run by default?

options.rationale: Correct: same-stage jobs run in parallel; stages run in sequence.

options.text: Strictly one after another in file order
options.rationale: Same-stage jobs are parallel, not sequential.
All jobs in the stage run.

options.text: They never run until the pipeline is approved
options.rationale: No approval is required for normal jobs.

items.explanation: Correct: same-stage jobs run in parallel; stages run in sequence.

items.stem: Which practices keep a GitLab CI pipeline secure and efficient? (Select TWO)

options.text: Store secrets as masked, protected CI/CD variables
options.rationale: Correct: masked protected variables keep secrets out of the repo and logs.

options.text: Use rules to run deploy jobs only on the intended branch
options.rationale: Correct: conditional rules avoid running jobs where they do not belong.
Hard-coding secrets exposes them in version control.

options.text: Deploy straight to production on every commit with no gate
options.rationale: Unreviewed automatic production deploys are risky.

items.explanation: Correct: masked protected variables keep secrets out of the repo and logs.; Correct: conditional rules avoid running jobs where they do not belong.

items.stem: When should you use artifacts rather than cache to move a build output to a later job?

options.text: When a later job depends on that output as a required input
options.rationale: Correct: artifacts reliably pass required outputs between jobs; cache is a best-effort speed-up.

options.text: Whenever you want to reduce dependency download time
options.rationale: That is the role of cache, not artifacts.
Secrets belong in variables, not artifacts.

options.text: Never; cache and artifacts are identical
options.rationale: They serve different purposes and guarantees.

items.explanation: Correct: artifacts reliably pass required outputs between jobs; cache is a best-effort speed-up.
